episode.title: Restore interactive terminal state before exiting on an uncaught exception
episode.before: At first parent 64882c6a516c6fe0e207ee3b114704f965e4eef6, interactive startup registered signal and terminal-stream error handlers, but no uncaughtException handler. An uncaught asynchronous throw could therefore terminate the process while the TUI still owned a raw-mode terminal with the cursor hidden and terminal input protocols enabled.
episode.after: At pinned ref 5998b579585d62491541ee44ef6451dc8695bb86, interactive mode prepends a lifecycle-managed uncaughtException listener. Its crash finalizer prevents re-entry, unregisters handlers, attempts to kill tracked detached children, attempts TUI shutdown to restore terminal state, reports the error, and exits with status 1.
episode.diff: The implementation adds 37 lines to packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts: a dedicated uncaughtCrash finalizer and an uncaughtException listener installed by registerSignalHandlers and removed through signalCleanupHandlers. No test file changed in the pinned first-parent diff.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned merge commit resolves PR 4426 with subject 'fix(coding-agent): restore terminal on uncaught exception' and changes one implementation file by 37 insertions.
The first-parent interactive-mode implementation registered SIGTERM, non-Windows SIGHUP, stdout error, and stderr error handlers, but contained no uncaughtException listener or crash finalizer.
evidence_units.source: git show 64882c6a516c6fe0e207ee3b114704f965e4eef6:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts, registerSignalHandlers and adjacent shutdown methods

evidence_units.claim: The change adds uncaughtCrash(error), which guards against repeated shutdown, marks shutdown active, independently attempts handler removal, detached-child cleanup, and ui.stop(), logs the exception, and exits with status 1.
registerSignalHandlers now prepends an uncaughtException listener that delegates to uncaughtCrash and records a matching process.off cleanup callback in signalCleanupHandlers.
Interactive initialization calls registerSignalHandlers before starting the UI, so the uncaught-exception listener is active while the TUI owns terminal state.
Normal shutdown and stop paths call unregisterSignalHandlers, which executes and clears all recorded cleanup callbacks, including removal of the new uncaughtException listener.
evidence_units.source: git show 5998b579585d62491541ee44ef6451dc8695bb86:packages/coding-agent/src/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts, shutdown, stop, registerSignalHandlers, and unregisterSignalHandlers

evidence_units.claim: At the pinned ref, TUI.stop shows the cursor and delegates to terminal.stop; terminal.stop disables bracketed paste and keyboard protocols, removes input handlers, pauses stdin, and restores the prior raw-mode state.
evidence_units.source: git show 5998b579585d62491541ee44ef6451dc8695bb86:packages/tui/src/tui.ts, TUI.stop; git show 5998b579585d62491541ee44ef6451dc8695bb86:packages/tui/src/terminal.ts, ProcessTerminal.stop

evidence_units.claim: The implementation commit describes the failure as an uncaught throw, commonly from an extension's asynchronous child-process exit callback, leaving stdin raw and the cursor hidden; it distinguishes this live-terminal case from dead-terminal SIGHUP or EIO handling.
The pinned first-parent diff changes only interactive-mode.ts and adds no automated regression test for the uncaught-exception terminal-restoration path.
git diff --check reports no whitespace errors for the pinned first-parent change.

candidate_atomics.name: scope-uncaught-failure-handler-to-interactive-lifecycle
candidate_atomics.title: Scope the uncaught-failure handler to the interactive lifecycle
candidate_atomics.description: Install the last-resort handler before terminal ownership begins and remove it through the same cleanup registry used by other process handlers.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure uncaught failures are intercepted only while the interactive terminal lifecycle is active, without leaking duplicate or stale process listeners.
semantic_action.pre_state: Interactive mode registers process handlers before starting the TUI, but uncaught exceptions bypass its cleanup lifecycle.
semantic_action.post_state: A highest-priority uncaught-exception listener is active during interactive operation and is removed whenever registered handlers are unregistered.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect initialization ordering, prependListener registration, matching process.off cleanup, and cleanup-registry reset.

candidate_atomics.name: finalize-live-terminal-on-uncaught-failure
candidate_atomics.title: Finalize a live terminal before fatal exit
candidate_atomics.description: On an uncaught failure, enter a guarded terminal state, perform independent best-effort cleanup operations, report the error, and terminate nonzero.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent a fatal asynchronous throw from leaving the user's terminal in raw mode, cursor-hidden, or protocol-enabled state.
semantic_action.pre_state: The interactive UI owns a still-live terminal when an uncaught exception reaches the process boundary.
semantic_action.post_state: Before nonzero process exit, repeated finalization is blocked and terminal restoration, detached-child cleanup, and handler removal have each been attempted without one cleanup failure suppressing the others.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the shutdown guard, isolated try blocks, ui.stop terminal-restoration contract, diagnostic output, and final exit status.

candidate_workflows.name: restore-interactive-terminal-on-uncaught-failure
candidate_workflows.title: Restore an interactive terminal on an uncaught process failure
candidate_workflows.description: Add a lifecycle-scoped process boundary that routes uncaught failures through a guarded, best-effort terminal finalizer before fatal exit.

workflow_graph.goal: An uncaught failure during interactive operation exits nonzero without leaving the live terminal in application-controlled state.
when_to_use: A long-running interactive process enables raw input, hides the cursor, or enables terminal protocols that ordinary process termination will not reliably restore.
Asynchronous callbacks or extension code can throw outside local try/catch boundaries while the terminal remains connected.
anti_goals: Do not convert uncaught failures into continued execution after potentially inconsistent process state.
Do not run normal terminal writes when the terminal is already known to be dead or disconnected.
Do not replace graceful shutdown or signal-specific cleanup paths with the last-resort crash path.
not_applicable_when: The program does not acquire persistent terminal state requiring restoration.
The failure path proves the terminal is unavailable, so restoration writes could recursively fail.
The exception is locally recoverable and does not require process termination.
workflow_graph.entry_state: Interactive mode has started or is about to start, and process-level uncaught throws currently bypass terminal restoration.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The uncaught-failure listener is lifecycle-scoped, and any intercepted fatal throw attempts independent resource cleanup and terminal restoration before diagnostic output and nonzero exit.

steps.condition: The interactive component owns terminal state and lacks a process-level uncaught-failure boundary.
steps.validation: Registration occurs before UI start, uses priority ordering, and has a matching cleanup callback exercised by handler unregistration.

steps.condition: An uncaught failure occurs while the terminal is still live.
steps.validation: The handler blocks re-entry, attempts each cleanup independently, invokes the terminal restoration primitive, reports the original error, and exits nonzero.

validation_ladder: Static diff validation: confirm the first-parent change adds only the crash finalizer and lifecycle-managed listener without whitespace errors.
Lifecycle validation: confirm initialization installs the listener before UI start and normal cleanup removes it.
Resource-contract validation: confirm the invoked UI stop operation restores the cursor and delegates to terminal cleanup that disables protocols and restores raw mode.
Deferred behavioral validation: trigger an uncaught asynchronous throw under a pseudo-terminal and assert nonzero exit plus restored terminal settings and cursor state.
stop_conditions: Stop if no reliable process-level uncaught-failure interception point exists.
Stop if the available cleanup primitive writes to a terminal that may already be dead; use the established dead-terminal emergency path instead.
Stop if listener removal cannot be tied to the interactive component's normal lifecycle.
Do not claim behavioral regression coverage until a pseudo-terminal test or equivalent runtime oracle is present.
unresolved_or_deferred: No automated test was added for the new crash path.
The pinned evidence does not show a pseudo-terminal reproduction proving terminal settings after the fatal exit.
Cleanup failures are intentionally swallowed, so the implementation guarantees best-effort attempts rather than verified restoration.

unresolved_questions: Can a deterministic pseudo-terminal regression test trigger an asynchronous uncaught throw and assert restored raw mode, visible cursor, disabled bracketed paste and keyboard protocols, detached-child cleanup, and exit status 1?
Should diagnostic writes also be guarded against stderr failure, given this handler runs at the final process boundary?
